scope: Part I v1.6 aligns Abstract/Introduction with the body: connected smooth projective reduced SNC ample pairs, n>=1, empty versus nonempty boundary, component-labelled multidegree complexes, metric versus ordinary-volume inputs and convergent centers. It makes raw/probability face-mass normalization explicit, proves a logarithmic obstruction to meromorphic continuation under ordinary volume-IRFA, and separates compact subcritical parameter uniformity from stronger continuation assumptions. Part II v2.1 aligns fully marked oriented residual periods and stable references, with n>=2 for nonempty-face translation and n=1 retained as its separate identity case. Existing distance, measure, moving/link and Chern-Weil proofs remain in place; this revision is a selected scope/interface and new-example audit, not a complete proof or priority certification.

current_revision.mathematical_scope: The public statements now explicitly distinguish metric-IRFA, ordinary volume-IRFA, bounded-primitive intersection theory and residual/angular L1 polyhomogeneity. Raw KE face mass m_F=(2pi)^n(L^(n-k).F)/(n-k)! is divided by total volume for probability-normalized data; normalized face masses do not form a probability partition. The abstract cusp measure e^(-t)(1+1/t)dt dtheta/(2pi) has Abel coefficient 1 and a logarithm after subtraction of its principal pole, so cannot continue meromorphically across the critical point. This is not asserted to be KE volume. Part II complex periods require factor/cusp labels and Kahler orientation; its generic unoriented theorem retains all labels, uses all curve factors, and recovers the arrangement only up to global conjugation. The pre-existing n=1 identity case is separate from nonempty-face translation. Previous selected proof audits remain valid without adding family-uniform conclusions.
